finding.claim: Attacker-controlled YAML passed to Mail::Message.from_yaml can set @delivery_method to a Mail::Sendmail whose settings[:location] is an arbitrary program, giving command execution on deliver!. Conditional on the app loading message YAML from attacker-influenced storage.
finding.source: YAML string argument to Message.from_yaml (also Part.from_yaml, which inherits it)
finding.sink: IO.popen(command) in Mail::Sendmail#popen, where command[0] is settings[:location] (sendmail.rb:72,80), reached via message.rb:269 delivery_method.deliver!

trace.note: safe_load permitted_classes includes Mail::Sendmail and Mail::FileDelivery
safe_load invoked with those permitted classes; object revival of permitted classes sets ivars
any key starting with '@' is accepted with no allowlist

finding.guards_checked: safe_load blocks arbitrary classes but permits the delivery classes whose settings are paths; array argv avoids a shell but does not restrict argv[0]; '--' guards only recipients; SmtpEnvelope CR/LF check (smtp_envelope.rb:50) does not apply to the delivery method. No allowlist on @-prefixed keys. Not verified by execution (no shell available).

finding.claim: POP3 over TLS disables server certificate verification, so credentials sent at line 133 can be captured by an on-path attacker.
finding.source: Network position (MITM); app config enable_ssl: true
finding.sink: Net::POP3 start(user_name, password) over an unverified TLS session (pop3.rb:133)

trace.note: pop3.start sends USER/PASS over that connection

finding.guards_checked: No verify_mode option is exposed for POP3; VERIFY_NONE is hardcoded. Not verified by execution.

finding.claim: IMAPS and STARTTLS connections are created with verify=false, so server certificates are not verified and an on-path attacker can capture IMAP credentials and mail.
finding.source: Network position (MITM); app config enable_ssl or enable_starttls

trace.note: Net::IMAP.new(address, port, enable_ssl, nil, false): fifth positional argument is verify=false
imap.starttls runs on the same unverified connection when enable_starttls

finding.guards_checked: No verify option exposed for IMAP. Signature inferred from the standard net-imap library, not confirmed against the installed version.

finding.claim: Attachment filenames from the sender's Content-Disposition/Content-Type are returned unsanitized (no basename or traversal stripping); apps that write attachments to disk using part.filename get path traversal. Conditional on app code doing that. Related path-reading APIs (add_file at message.rb:1764-1769, attachments_list.rb:49-50, Mail.read at mail.rb:168-170) are API hazards if passed untrusted input.
finding.source: Sender-controlled Content-Disposition filename parameter in an email
finding.sink: Application file write using part.filename (not in this library); library paths listed in the claim are filesystem reads

trace.note: decode_encode(filename, :decode) only decodes RFC2047/encoded forms; no basename

finding.guards_checked: decode_encode only; no path stripping in the library. Whether the calling app sanitizes is not known from this code.
